    Getting started¶

    This tutorial builds a specification, draws graphs from it with different seeds and specifications, compares them, and saves one. It runs in a few seconds.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import bipgen
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd import bipgen

    A specification¶

    A dictionary with the layout of the YAML format: 2000 BCN and 3000 TGT in the unit disk, lognormal target degrees, a Gaussian kernel of scale 0.12 and 5% background edges.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    base = {
    "sizes": {"n_bcn": 2000, "n_tgt": 3000},
    "degrees": {"distribution": "lognormal",
                "bcn": {"median": 15, "sigma": 0.5},
                "tgt": {"sigma": 0.6}},  # shape only: scale set by the BCN total
    "edges": {"model": "kernel", "kernel": "gaussian", "scale": 0.12},
    "background": {"model": "uniform", "ratio": 0.05},
}
spec = bipgen.spec_from_dict(base)
spec.to_dict()
    base = { "sizes": {"n_bcn": 2000, "n_tgt": 3000}, "degrees": {"distribution": "lognormal", "bcn": {"median": 15, "sigma": 0.5}, "tgt": {"sigma": 0.6}}, # shape only: scale set by the BCN total "edges": {"model": "kernel", "kernel": "gaussian", "scale": 0.12}, "background": {"model": "uniform", "ratio": 0.05}, } spec = bipgen.spec_from_dict(base) spec.to_dict()
    Out[2]:

    One realization¶

    The seed comes from the specification (42 by default) unless it is given in the call. info records the seed, the target number of edges, the expected number after clipping probabilities at 1, the convergence of Sinkhorn scaling, and the seconds spent in each step (timing).

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    graph = bipgen.generate(spec)
print(graph)
graph.info
    graph = bipgen.generate(spec) print(graph) graph.info
    BipartiteGraph(n_bcn=2000, n_tgt=3000, dim=2, edges=33684 geometric + 1684 background, seed=42)

    Seeds¶

    The same seed gives the same graph; other seeds give other realizations of the same ensemble.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    same = bipgen.generate(spec, seed=42)
print("same seed, edges that differ:", (graph.biadjacency != same.biadjacency).nnz)

ensemble = [bipgen.generate(spec, seed=s) for s in range(5)]
print("edges in five realizations:", [g.n_edges for g in ensemble])
    same = bipgen.generate(spec, seed=42) print("same seed, edges that differ:", (graph.biadjacency != same.biadjacency).nnz) ensemble = [bipgen.generate(spec, seed=s) for s in range(5)] print("edges in five realizations:", [g.n_edges for g in ensemble])
    same seed, edges that differ: 0

    edges in five realizations: [35003, 34436, 34659, 35267, 33796]

    Different specifications¶

    The same sizes and degrees with a short kernel, a long one, and the long one with more background edges. Sinkhorn scaling matches the target degrees before probabilities are clipped at 1: with the short kernel, clipping removes part of the edges, and expected_edges measures it.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    variants = {
    "scale 0.10": {**base, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.10}},
    "scale 0.25": {**base, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.25}},
    "scale 0.25, 20% background": {**base, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.25},
                                   "background": {"model": "uniform", "ratio": 0.2}},
}
graphs = {name: bipgen.generate(bipgen.spec_from_dict(v)) for name, v in variants.items()}
for name, g in graphs.items():
    print(f"{name:28s} {g}  expected / target edges = "
          f"{g.info['expected_edges'] / g.info['target_edges']:.3f}")
    variants = { "scale 0.10": {**base, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.10}}, "scale 0.25": {**base, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.25}}, "scale 0.25, 20% background": {**base, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.25}, "background": {"model": "uniform", "ratio": 0.2}}, } graphs = {name: bipgen.generate(bipgen.spec_from_dict(v)) for name, v in variants.items()} for name, g in graphs.items(): print(f"{name:28s} {g} expected / target edges = " f"{g.info['expected_edges'] / g.info['target_edges']:.3f}")
    scale 0.10                   BipartiteGraph(n_bcn=2000, n_tgt=3000, dim=2, edges=32669 geometric + 1633 background, seed=42)  expected / target edges = 0.948
scale 0.25                   BipartiteGraph(n_bcn=2000, n_tgt=3000, dim=2, edges=34577 geometric + 1728 background, seed=42)  expected / target edges = 0.999
scale 0.25, 20% background   BipartiteGraph(n_bcn=2000, n_tgt=3000, dim=2, edges=34577 geometric + 6915 background, seed=42)  expected / target edges = 0.999

    Comparing graphs¶

    One row per graph: nodes and a subset of edges, edge lengths, and the degree distributions of the two sides, realized against target. A longer kernel gives longer edges; background edges have lengths unrelated to distance and add to the degrees.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(graphs), 4, figsize=(15, 3.6 * len(graphs)))
for row, (name, g) in zip(axes, graphs.items()):
    bipgen.plot_graph(g, ax=row[0], max_edges=2000, node_size=1)
    bipgen.plot_edge_lengths(g, ax=row[1])
    bipgen.plot_degrees(g, axes=row[2:])
    row[0].set_title(f"{name}\n{row[0].get_title()}", fontsize=9)
fig.tight_layout()
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(graphs), 4, figsize=(15, 3.6 * len(graphs))) for row, (name, g) in zip(axes, graphs.items()): bipgen.plot_graph(g, ax=row[0], max_edges=2000, node_size=1) bipgen.plot_edge_lengths(g, ax=row[1]) bipgen.plot_degrees(g, axes=row[2:]) row[0].set_title(f"{name}\n{row[0].get_title()}", fontsize=9) fig.tight_layout()

    The same summary statistics on each graph. To test an observed graph against an ensemble, see Presets and comparison.

    k nearest neighbours¶

    Each BCN links to its k nearest TGT; no degree section is needed.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    knn = bipgen.spec_from_dict({"sizes": {"n_bcn": 1500, "n_tgt": 1500},
                             "edges": {"model": "knn", "k": 6}})
g = bipgen.generate(knn)
bipgen.plot_degrees(g);
    knn = bipgen.spec_from_dict({"sizes": {"n_bcn": 1500, "n_tgt": 1500}, "edges": {"model": "knn", "k": 6}}) g = bipgen.generate(knn) bipgen.plot_degrees(g);

    Spatially correlated density¶

    Cell counts with coefficient of variation 0.8, arranged to bring the spatial correlation between nearby cells (Moran's I) at lags 1 and 2 towards the target. The correlogram reached is in info.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 5))
for ax, rho in zip(axes, ([0.1, 0.05], [0.7, 0.5])):
    s = bipgen.spec_from_dict({**base, "positions": {"method": "metropolis", "density": {
        "occupancy": {"source": "gamma", "cv": 0.8}, "correlogram": rho, "sweeps": 200}}})
    g = bipgen.generate(s)
    bipgen.plot_graph(g, ax=ax, max_edges=0, node_size=2)
    ax.set_title(f"target {rho}, reached {np.round(g.info['correlogram'], 2).tolist()}",
                 fontsize=9)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 5)) for ax, rho in zip(axes, ([0.1, 0.05], [0.7, 0.5])): s = bipgen.spec_from_dict({**base, "positions": {"method": "metropolis", "density": { "occupancy": {"source": "gamma", "cv": 0.8}, "correlogram": rho, "sweeps": 200}}}) g = bipgen.generate(s) bipgen.plot_graph(g, ax=ax, max_edges=0, node_size=2) ax.set_title(f"target {rho}, reached {np.round(g.info['correlogram'], 2).tolist()}", fontsize=9)

    3D¶

    The domain becomes the unit ball.

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    g3 = bipgen.generate(bipgen.spec_from_dict(
    {**base, "dim": 3, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.2}}))
print(g3)
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(5.5, 5.5))
bipgen.plot_graph(g3, ax=fig.add_subplot(projection="3d"), max_edges=0, node_size=2);
    g3 = bipgen.generate(bipgen.spec_from_dict( {**base, "dim": 3, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.2}})) print(g3) fig = plt.figure(figsize=(5.5, 5.5)) bipgen.plot_graph(g3, ax=fig.add_subplot(projection="3d"), max_edges=0, node_size=2);
    BipartiteGraph(n_bcn=2000, n_tgt=3000, dim=3, edges=33307 geometric + 1665 background, seed=42)

    Spatially correlated densities work in 3D too, on a grid of cubic cells clipped to the unit ball. A thin slice through the centre shows the clusters better than the whole cloud.

    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    s3 = bipgen.spec_from_dict({**base, "dim": 3, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.2},
                            "positions": {"method": "metropolis", "density": {
                                "correlogram": [0.7, 0.5], "sweeps": 200}}})
g3 = bipgen.generate(s3)
pts = np.vstack([g3.pos_bcn, g3.pos_tgt])
slab = pts[np.abs(pts[:, 2]) < 0.1]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 4.5))
ax.scatter(slab[:, 0], slab[:, 1], s=3, color="#2a78d6", linewidths=0)
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.set_title(f"thin slice |z| < 0.1 of a 3D correlated density, {len(slab)} nodes", fontsize=9);
    s3 = bipgen.spec_from_dict({**base, "dim": 3, "edges": {"model": "kernel", "scale": 0.2}, "positions": {"method": "metropolis", "density": { "correlogram": [0.7, 0.5], "sweeps": 200}}}) g3 = bipgen.generate(s3) pts = np.vstack([g3.pos_bcn, g3.pos_tgt]) slab = pts[np.abs(pts[:, 2]) < 0.1] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 4.5)) ax.scatter(slab[:, 0], slab[:, 1], s=3, color="#2a78d6", linewidths=0) ax.set_aspect("equal") ax.set_title(f"thin slice |z| < 0.1 of a 3D correlated density, {len(slab)} nodes", fontsize=9);

    Saving¶

    One directory per graph: edge table, node table, specification and diagnostics.

    In [13]:
    Copied! 
    import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = bipgen.save(graph, Path(tmp) / "graph_042")
    print(sorted(p.name for p in path.iterdir()))
    again = bipgen.load(path)
print(again)
print("edges that differ after reloading:", (again.biadjacency != graph.biadjacency).nnz)
    import tempfile from pathlib import Path with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp: path = bipgen.save(graph, Path(tmp) / "graph_042") print(sorted(p.name for p in path.iterdir())) again = bipgen.load(path) print(again) print("edges that differ after reloading:", (again.biadjacency != graph.biadjacency).nnz)
    ['edges.csv', 'info.json', 'nodes.csv', 'spec.yaml']
